title: The Hut in the Forest variant

keywords: the hut in the forest variant
full_text:
Three sisters were sent into the deep forest to deliver bread to their father. The two eldest lost their way, found an old thatched hut occupied by an elderly sage and his domestic beasts—a hen, a rooster, and a cow. The selfish elder daughters demanded supper and comfortable beds, eating their fill while ignoring the hungry animals. The elderly host sent them down into a cold cellar for their callous arrogance.

The youngest daughter, gentle and observant, arrived at the hut on the third evening. Before she touched a single morsel of porridge, she greeted the animals affectionately, fed sweet grain to the birds, and carried an armful of fresh clover to the cow. She ensured their water trough was filled and stroked their heads with genuine love.

When morning dawned, she was awakened by the singing of courtiers. The rustic hut had transformed into a glorious crystal palace! The elderly sage was revealed as an enchanted prince, freed from a century-long curse because a maiden had appeared whose compassionate heart honored humble creatures before herself.

The grateful prince married the maiden in royal splendor, while her older sisters were released and sent home with a wise lesson in true courtesy and kindness.
moral: Those who show loving kindness to all creatures, big and small, unlock the greatest blessings of life.
